newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: SOCCER-COSTA RICA APPOINT NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COSTA RICA APPOINT NEW COACH.

text.p: Costa Rica named Spaniard Juan Luis Hernandez as their new national soccer coach on Tuesday.
Hernandez, currently in charge of first division Cartagines, became the team's third coach this year following the dismissal of Argentina's Horacio Cordero.
Cordero was sacked last Thursday in the wake of a 0-0 home draw with El Salvador in a World Cup qualifier.

Brazil's Valdeir Vieira, who guided the team to the final stage of the CONCACAF qualifying tournament, was dismissed in January when he refused to drop a claim for unpaid wages against a local club he previously coached.
Hernandez blamed indiscipline for a disappointing sequence of recent results and promised to impose tougher rules on the squad.

Costa Rica, who reached the last 16 on their only World Cup finals appearance in 1990, are second in the final stage qualifying competition with eight points from six matches, but three of their last four games are away.

The top three teams in the group, which also includes Mexico, United States, Canada, El Salvador and Jamaica, will go to France. Mexico lead with 11 points from five matches, while only three points separate the other five teams.
